TASK: rebalance the CI coverage shards by measured test time.

PROBLEM: tests/conftest.py (pytest_collection_modifyitems, the `shard_count > 1` block near line 284) assigns tests to shards round-robin over node IDs sorted alphabetically. The last CI run (4 shards, .github/workflows/test.yml 'test-shard', `pytest -n 4 --shard-index N --shard-count 4`) took 1m43s, 1m55s, 2m37s and 3m29s, so one shard is about twice as slow as another. The tier report (--tier-report) is empty under xdist, so there is no stored timing.

OWNED FILES (edit nothing else): tests/conftest.py, tests/shard_durations.json (new), tests/test_shard_balance.py (new), docs/testing-runbook.md (edit the EXISTING shard line/entry in place, at most two sentences; do not append results, counts or dates).

DO:
1. Measure: run the full suite once with per-test durations, e.g. `PYTHONPATH=$PWD TMPDIR=/tmp /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider -n 4 --durations=0 --durations-min=0 2>&1 > /tmp/durations.txt` (setup+call+teardown lines are all printed; sum them per test FILE). Do the measurement with the same -n 4 the CI shards use, on an otherwise idle machine if possible; run it twice and average per file to damp noise.
2. Write tests/shard_durations.json: {"version": 1, "files": {"tests/test_x.py": seconds_float, ...}} for every test file, rounded to 2 decimals, sorted keys.
3. Replace the round-robin with a deterministic whole-FILE assignment: group the collected items by file path, take each file's weight from the json (a file missing from the json gets the median weight of the listed files; a file listed but not collected is ignored), sort files by weight descending then path, and assign each file greedily to the currently lightest shard (longest-processing-time rule; ties go to the lowest shard index). Keep all items of a file in one shard so module and session fixtures are built once per shard. Every collected item must land in exactly one shard. Keep the existing option names, validation and deselect logic; shard_count == 1 behaviour is unchanged. If one file is heavier than 40% of total weight, split THAT file by node ID round-robin among shards instead (explain in a comment); otherwise never split a file.
4. tests/test_shard_balance.py (fast, hermetic): (a) every collected node ID is in exactly one of 4 shards and the union equals the full collection (use pytest's collection through `pytester` if the repo already uses it, otherwise import the assignment as a pure function from conftest or a small helper module you add under tests/ and test it on the real json plus the real file list); (b) predicted shard weights from the json differ by less than 15 percent between the heaviest and lightest; (c) a test file absent from the json still gets assigned; (d) assignment is deterministic across two calls. Factor the assignment into a pure function so these tests need no subprocess.
5. Verify balance for real: for N in 0..3 run `pytest --collect-only -q --shard-index N --shard-count 4 | tail -1` and confirm counts sum to the full count, then time one `-n 4` run of each shard (--cov not needed) and write the four wall times to the notes. If the slowest is more than 1.3x the fastest, re-measure and refine weights once.
